title: Renewals window
goal: Work every contract in the window to a decision — send it for renewal or let it lapse — until the window is empty.
primaryQuestion: Which contract do I handle first?
_why: Nobody searches this screen (brief, verbatim) and the set is given, so this is the taxonomy's worklist: ListPageTemplate with no toolbar, no FilterBar, no SearchInput. The moment someone asks for a filter, the archetype flips to list and this spec is wrong on purpose, not silently.

zones.name: header
zones.purpose: The screen's name, with the count of contracts still awaiting review as a Badge beside the title (title is ReactNode; nothing renders under it). No creating action — the window is fed by end dates, not by people — and no filters, which is what keeps this a worklist.

zones.name: window
zones.answers: Which contract do I handle first?
zones.purpose: One row per contract, ordered by endDate ascending — soonest first, so reading order IS priority order and comparing annualValue and endDate across the whole window is a glance down two columns. A table, not cards, by R8 (a queue of records wants density and status) and R1's reason (six comparable fields want columns; cards would make comparing two contracts mean reading two paragraphs). Columns: id, counterparty, accountManager, annualValue (align end), endDate, status as a Badge, and the decision. An awaiting-review row carries its two decisions in place — Send for renewal and Let lapse, small, neither primary: they are peers and there are many per screen; a decided row shows its status and nothing pressable. The table sits in a Card flush inside a TableScroll, on the template's panels mode with stickyHeader, so only the rows scroll and the column names survive the scroll.

states.empty: EmptyState via the template's empty prop, icon=check_circle. The GOOD state: a window worked down to zero is the week's job done, and the copy says so — no action button, because nothing here creates contracts.
states.error: Not applicable while the rows are inline mock data; when the contract feed arrives this becomes an Alert tone=danger above the table with a retry, and this sentence is the reminder.

data: contracts: id, counterparty, accountManager, annualValue, endDate, status (awaiting-review | renewal-sent | lapsing) — 8-10 mock rows inline in the screen, spanning all three statuses so every row shape renders, decided in local state so the decisions really move a row
acceptance: Rows are ordered by endDate, soonest first, and nothing on the screen can reorder, filter or search them.
annualValue and endDate each line up in their own column; two contracts compare without moving the eyes off a column.
Both decisions sit on the row itself: deciding needs no dialog and no navigation, and the row's status changes where it stands.
Only awaiting-review rows carry the two decision buttons; decided rows show their status Badge and nothing pressable.
Only the rows scroll; the page header and the column header row stay put.
The empty window reads as the week's work done, never as an error.

behaviours.given: a contract whose status is awaiting-review
behaviours.when: the specialist presses Send for renewal on its row
behaviours.then: the same row now shows the renewal-sent Badge, its two decision buttons are gone, and no navigation happened
behaviours.why: The brief's central promise: the two decisions are applied in place.
behaviours.pendingReason: Delivered as a single screen file ahead of the product's own repo and test harness; the test lands with the first vitest setup, named renewals-window#send-for-renewal-in-place.

behaviours.given: a contract whose status is awaiting-review
behaviours.when: the specialist presses Let lapse on its row
behaviours.then: the same row now shows the lapsing Badge, its two decision buttons are gone, and no navigation happened
behaviours.why: The other half of the same promise — lapsing is a decision taken, not an omission.
behaviours.pendingReason: Same harness gap as send-for-renewal-in-place; the test carries renewals-window#let-lapse-in-place.

behaviours.given: a window with no contracts in it
behaviours.then: the empty state says the week's work is done, styled as success of the process, not as missing data
behaviours.why: When the window is empty, that is the good state (brief, verbatim).
behaviours.pendingReason: Same harness gap; the test carries renewals-window#empty-window-is-done.

openQuestions: Does a decided contract stay in the window with its new status until the week rolls, or leave the list at once? Built as: it stays, so the specialist keeps the week's record on screen; the model carries the same question.
Whether Let lapse ever needs a confirmation. Built without one — it is reversible upstream and the audience lives here daily — but the first mis-click story reopens it.
